rubric_items.reason: All 10 acceptance criteria have at least one test: S-1 AC1-AC5, S-2 AC1-AC2 and S-3 AC1-AC3. REQ-1..REQ-10 are traced. TP-14 now tests the upper bound of S-1/AC3.
Counts, bounds and list matching are tested at API integration level. The tile title, link, reload and zero value are tested at web unit level. There are no e2e or manual tests.
Both boundaries are tested (TP-3 below, TP-14 above), plus a zero edge case (TP-13) and a regression test (TP-15). The expected result of the negative test TP-12 is still not backed by any input.

Uses the strategy's tools (Vitest, Supertest, fixed clock, jsdom, Testing Library), the api/test and web __tests__ folders, and names that start with requirement IDs. The new file is named and the plan says why it needs its own database.

Titles are specific and start with requirement IDs. The new file is named. The expected result of TP-12, 'yields no dashboard counts', is vague: it could mean a 400, zero totals or an empty body, so a tester cannot run it as written.

findings.text: TP-12 no longer expects a 400, but 'yields no dashboard counts' is still not stated by any input. C9 only lists the three periods. The existing DSH-7 test says the period defaults to Today, which hints at different behaviour. TP-12 also maps to S-1/AC4, which is about changing between valid periods.

cites.quote: a period other than Today, Last 7 days or Last 30 days yields no dashboard counts
DSH-7: the period is Today, Last 7 days or Last 30 days, default Today
Given the period is Today, when staff change it to Last 7 days or Last 30 days, then the No-shows count updates to that period.

findings.suggested_fix: Drop TP-12 and rely on TP-15 (the DSH-7 regression), or state the router's current response to an unknown period with a citation and assert exactly that.

status = 'NO_SHOW' AND starts_at >= period start AND starts_at < end of today
